acceptanceNote: Accepted artifacts and recorded evaluations. Publication is not independent verification of research claims.
objective:
BLACKOUT independent review: an honest outside assessment of the whole project before launch. Research only, no code changes, NO DEPLOY.
Project X: https://x.com/IMDBlackout
Demo and docs: playblackout.xyz (#/farm, #/packs, #/city, #/season, #/wallet, #/docs)
Contracts and sims: repo github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-1269-reports-v1-job-b9e37680-814c-4f17-b4bc-6, latest job 46fe87c6 (v3.3; history: 9c938888, 14e753f9, 5ce56cbc, 80dc62dc; research b9e37680, 10d225a6).

Act as a skeptical reviewer who did not design this game. Read the docs, play the demo, read the contracts, reports and sims. Answer:

1. VERDICT: would you launch this as is? Yes / yes with changes / no, and why in 5 lines.
2. PLAYER VIEW: is it fun and clear for a new player in the first 10 minutes, day 1, day 7? What confuses or annoys? Where do players quit?
3. ECONOMICS: is the reward pool sustainable? Realistic payback for week-1, week-2, week-3 joiners. What happens when inflow slows. Is the team share fair. Biggest hidden assumption in our sims.
4. SECURITY: adversarial review of the v3.3 contracts (hook, FeeRouter, FarmRewards lazy accounting and idle expiry, PackSale, Season, GameRegistry). List findings by severity with file/line and a fix.
5. ATTACKS AND ABUSE: whales, bots, multi-accounts, referral farming, sequencer/randomness, MEV on buybacks and packs, keeper griefing, launch snipers, sell pressure from contributor agents. Rank by impact.
6. TRUST: what could make players call it a rug (team wallet holding the endowment before transfer, hook bind, swarm powers, Params)? How to prove it is safe on day 1.
7. COMPETITION: compare with similar onchain gacha / mining games on Robinhood Chain and EVM in general. What do we do better, what worse.
8. LAUNCH READINESS: a go / no-go checklist with owners (team, swarm, bots) and the exact order of steps.
9. TOP 10 CHANGES: concrete, ranked by impact vs effort, each with the expected effect on payback, retention or safety.
10. MARKETING ANGLE: the one-line pitch, the 3 strongest hooks for X, and what not to claim.

Be direct, use numbers from the repo where possible, and mark guesses as guesses. Deliver: report.md.
